title: HINT for Lawyers — drafts stay inside the red lines
metaDescription: Keep matter facts, clauses, sources and red lines beside legal documents so assistants draft from declared positions and expose gaps.
h1: Your assistant drafts fast. HINT keeps it inside the matter's red lines.
intro: HINT is a folder of plain-text matter notes beside your documents. Your assistant reads the notes that apply before drafting and sees the parties, defined terms, sources and positions it must not cross.

situations.before: A draft fills an absent commercial term with plausible language.
situations.body: The assistant asks for the missing duration or remedy instead of choosing one for the client.

situations.before: A clause uses a source or citation nobody verified.
situations.body: Sources stay attached to the provision they support, and unsupported citations are reported for counsel to resolve.

situations.before: Terms from another matter bleed into the current draft.
situations.after: Each client stays in its own scope
situations.body: Folder inheritance carries firm policy down while keeping another client's facts outside the current matter.

example.intro: The Pearson Specter Litt demo records Acme's confidentiality position in the matter folder.
lines: The Employee has access to Acme's source code, systems, and product plans.
Non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of Acme.
example.after: It drafts using the declared definition and exceptions, preserves defined-term discipline, and flags any commercial position that the matter has not supplied.

never: Invent a party, fact, citation or negotiated position.
Carry one client's matter knowledge into another client's folder.
Present generated language as legal advice or as ready for signature.
disclaimer: HINT does not practice law. Drafts and reviews are work product for qualified counsel and require professional judgment before use.

faq.a: No. It supplies declared matter context to an assistant; licensed counsel remains responsible for every legal judgment.
It tells the assistant that authority must come from declared sources and turns missing support into a gap, but counsel still verifies every citation.

faq.q: Can firm policy and matter terms coexist?
faq.a: Yes. Firm rules can live above client folders; client and document notes add narrower context below them.

keywordDescriptions.matter: Sets the client, purpose and boundary of the legal work.
keywordDescriptions.party: Names a party and its role in the matter.
keywordDescriptions.clause: Records a clause that the document must contain.
keywordDescriptions.obligation: States an action a party is required to perform.
keywordDescriptions.right: States an entitlement and the conditions around it.
keywordDescriptions.source: Identifies authority or evidence rather than inviting a citation guess.
keywordDescriptions.redline: Marks a position that drafting must not cross.
keywordDescriptions.never: States an unconditional prohibition for the assistant.
